title: GVR-ProtocolEval (repaired): Preregistered generate–validate–repair evaluation for NetOps safety across protocols and modalities
research_question: How much does a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline reduce operational-failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM-only generation, across protocol families and interaction modalities (CLI vs API), under controlled fault-injection?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The GVR pipeline yields a lower operational-failure rate than LLM-only generation across the confirmatory task bank (paired comparison).
H2: Residual GVR failures will be concentrated in vendor-syntax translation and verifier-coverage blind spots rather than core logical errors.
H3: GVR gains vary by interaction modality: API-mode runs will show smaller residual failure rates than CLI-mode runs given identical verifier capabilities.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How many repair iterations are typically required before verifier acceptance, and what is the distribution of iteration counts?
EQ2: Which specific syntactic translation patterns correlate with persistent GVR failures?
EQ3: How sensitive are primary results to verifier-rule coverage and to model nondeterminism controls?
benchmark_scope: Custom task bank (confirmatory) of intent-to-configuration tasks executed in a Mininet-based emulated testbed with scripted vendor-syntax templates (public-domain vendor examples sampled from vendor documentation and RFCs).
Fault-injection scenarios limited to link flaps, device restart, and config drift emulated within Mininet containers.
Evaluations bounded to the emulated device behaviors and public vendor examples; no private production devices are used.
model_scope: Hosted LLM API (single vendor endpoint) with temperature and seed controls as permitted by capability_manifest.
Deterministic local tooling for verifier and syntax translators executed on CPU (Docker containers).
transformation_scope: Text normalization, vendor-syntax templating, vendor-specific command rendering (template expansion), and verifier-rule extraction for deterministic checks.
primary_estimand: Paired mean difference in operational-failure indicator (1 if reachability loss or policy violation observed during deployment tests; 0 otherwise) between LLM-only and GVR pipelines, expressed as absolute and relative reduction with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
secondary_estimands: Per-protocol and per-modality paired mean differences (same metric as primary) with subgroup CIs.
Distribution of repair-iteration counts and median iterations to verifier acceptance.
Proportion of failures attributable to syntactic-translation vs verifier-coverage (automated classification rules).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory task bank: 200 tasks covering five protocol/focus categories (ACLs, static/dynamic routing, NAT, VLANs, service-ACL interactions) stratified across vendors and two interaction modalities (CLI, API). Each confirmatory task is executed once per pipeline variant in a paired design (LLM-only, LLM+single-pass verifier, GVR loop). Additionally, 50 exploratory tasks will be run for discovery analyses. Task-cluster mapping: 5 protocol groups × 2 modalities = 10 clusters; confirmatory tasks allocated approximately uniformly across clusters (20 tasks per cluster) producing per-cluster confirmatory n=20. Randomization: task order randomized with fixed seed; Dockerized Mininet testbed seeded for deterministic fault-injection schedules. Inclusion/exclusion: tasks that trigger infrastructure errors (container crashes) are excluded from primary analysis but logged and reported; infrastructure failures are treated separately from operational-failure outcomes.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired per-task differences in binary operational-failure outcome between LLM-only and GVR; estimate mean paired differences with 95% bootstrap CIs (10,000 bootstrap resamples, fixed RNG seed). Use Wilcoxon signed-rank test as a nonparametric confirmatory test; report exact p-values. Adjust for multiple subgroup tests (per-protocol) using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control at q=0.05. Secondary analyses: subgroup CIs, repair-iteration descriptive stats, automated failure-classification counts. All per-run raw artifacts and code for automated analyses (Dockerized) will be published to permit independent reanalysis. Exploratory findings labeled and distinguished from confirmatory claims.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is the paired LLM-only vs GVR comparison on the full confirmatory bank (one primary hypothesis). Secondary subgroup tests and exploratory analyses are multiplicity-adjusted as specified (Benjamini–Hochberg for subgroup tests). Report unadjusted exploratory statistics but label them exploratory.
missingness_plan: If a deployed run fails due to infrastructure error (container crash, Mininet failure), the run is logged as 'infrastructure failure' and excluded from the confirmatory binary outcome; the exclusion count and reasons are reported. All other task outputs are retained; missing verifier logs trigger automated re-execution up to the preregistered retry limit (see nondeterminism controls).

benchmark_names: Mininet emulation harness (Docker images, public vendor snippets)
risk_factors: Model memorization of public vendor configuration snippets leading to non-generalizable generation.
Overlap between task prompts and model training data (unknown to researchers) causing leakage.
Public example-based vendor templates may underrepresent private production idiosyncrasies.
detection_procedures: Exact-match and high-similarity checks against curated public corpus (vendor docs, RFCs) using deterministic string-hash and token-overlap thresholds; matches >80% token overlap flagged.
Automated similarity scoring (BLEU and longest-common-subsequence) between generated config and corpus; results recorded and flagged if above thresholds.
Record and publish all flagged items with hashes for independent verification.
item_flagging_rules: If generated configuration has >=80% token-level overlap with any single public-corpus document, flag the item and exclude it from the primary confirmatory analysis (treated in a sensitivity analysis).
If a task's prompt is detected to be present verbatim in the public corpus, flag the task and report separately.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis; results reported both with and without flagged exclusions as sensitivity analyses. All exclusions and their rationales are logged with reproducible hashes.
residual_uncertainty: Even with automated detection, undocumented model pretraining data overlap cannot be fully ruled out; this remains a noncritical external-validity limitation.
Emulated vendor snippets are sampled from public sources and may not represent private vendor idiosyncrasies.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended (balanced) scenario: confirmatory 200 tasks + exploratory 50 tasks; conservative average GVR repair iterations = 4 (so 5 model calls for GVR including initial generation); LLM-only and single-pass verifier each require 1 model call per task. Includes pilot warm-up calls and preregistration tuning budget.
models: Hosted LLM API (production endpoint; temperature and seed controls) — model calls counted
transformations: Prompt templating and normalization (no model calls)
Vendor-syntax templating and deterministic translator (no model calls)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task model-call arithmetic: per-task calls = LLM-only (1) + LLM+verifier (1) + GVR average (5) = 7 calls. Total tasks = 250 → 250×7 = 1750. Add 250 pilot/warm-up calls + 500 sensitivity/ablation calls = 2500 total planned model calls. This fits the capability_manifest limit (<=10000) and exceeds the power requirement (see power_plan).

budget_scenarios.description: High-powered scenario: enlarge confirmatory bank to 400 tasks (to increase subgroup power) with same per-task call assumptions; increased pilot and sensitivity budgets.
models: Hosted LLM API (production endpoint; temperature and seed controls)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task calls = 7. Total tasks = 500 (400 confirmatory +100 exploratory) → 500×7 = 3500. Add 500 pilot/sensitivity = 4000 planned calls. Within capability_manifest maximum (<=10000). Offers greater subgroup power at higher model-call budget.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute reduction in operational-failure rate (LLM-only minus GVR) across confirmatory tasks.
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 10 percentage points (e.g., from 30% baseline to 20%).
power_plan.clustering_unit: Task (each intent-to-configuration instance is a paired observation across pipelines).
power_plan.calculation_method: Conservative paired-to-independent approximation: two-sample independent-proportions formula used for an upper-bound sample estimate, then adjusted for expected within-task pairing correlation (ρ≈0.5). Independent-proportions estimate: n_per_group = ((Z_{1-α/2}+Z_{1-β})^2 * (p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2))) / d^2. Using α=0.05 (two-sided), power 0.80 → Z=1.96+0.84=2.80; p1=0.30, p2=0.20, d=0.10 → n_per_group_independent ≈ 290. Paired-design effective n ≈ n_per_group_independent * (1-ρ) ≈ 290*(1-0.5)=145 tasks. We preregister 200 confirmatory tasks to provide margin for exclusions and cluster-level subgroup analyses.
assumptions: Baseline operational-failure rate (LLM-only) ≈ 30% (conservative estimate from prototype literature and pilot runs).
Target absolute reduction d=10 percentage points is operationally meaningful and detectable.
Within-task paired correlation between pipeline outcomes ≈ 0.5 (moderate); sensitivity checks will evaluate ρ∈{0.3,0.5,0.7}.
Alpha=0.05 (two-sided); power target 0.80; bootstrap CI method for primary estimate with 10,000 resamples.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With 200 confirmatory tasks and assumed ρ=0.5, the minimum detectable absolute difference (two-sided, 80% power) is approximately 0.08–0.11 depending on exact baseline; sensitivity analyses will report MDE across ρ∈{0.3,0.5,0.7} and baseline p1∈{0.25,0.30,0.35}.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power/MDE with ρ=0.3 and ρ=0.7.
Report subgroup MDE for per-cluster n=20 (per-cluster confirmatory tasks) acknowledging lower power and labeling cluster results as exploratory unless powered.

transformation_families: Vendor-syntax templating (template expansion from canonical public snippets).
Verifier output parsing (deterministic parse to structured checks).
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip parser: generated config → deterministic parser → canonical internal representation → renderer → regenerated config; accept only if renderer output semantically matches the original under token-similarity ≥95%.
Automated unit tests for each template and translator using a public sample of vendor commands; unit-test suite executed in CI (Docker) with fixed seeds.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated configs failing deterministic parser or failing basic syntactic checks (missing required keywords) — these are auto-excluded from deployment and counted as verifier rejections.
Reject configs that exceed token-similarity thresholds to a public-corpus example (contamination rule) — flagged and excluded from primary analysis.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deeper checks on a reproducible random 10% audit sample of generated configs (seeded RNG); audits run via deterministic linting and semantic-diff tools. Audit results published.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Publish mapping rules and unit-test outputs; maintain a deterministic mapping manifest (intent → template id) with hashes for each mapping entry.
residual_risks: Semantic equivalence heuristics may miss subtle vendor idiosyncrasies; residual syntax/semantics mismatches possible.
Verification unit tests rely on public examples and may not capture private production edge cases.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Emulated vendor-syntax fidelity: despite sampling public vendor examples and adding template unit tests, emulation may not capture all production device idiosyncrasies (external-validity limitation).
Unknown overlap between model pretraining data and public vendor examples cannot be fully excluded; automated contamination detection mitigates but cannot prove absence.
Per-cluster subgroup power is limited (per-cluster confirmatory n=20); subgroup estimates will have wide CIs and are treated as secondary/exploratory unless pooled.
